messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: model-warmup-failures detected in us-west-2. model_id=redwood/myri-7b-q2a, failures=72 in 5m, symptom=container restarts + 5xx spike :rotating_light:
Maya: ack-ing. paging oncall... I'm oncall for infra this shift.
Maya: quick look — dashboards show 503s up from 0.7% -> 9% for routes using myri-7b-q2a, error rate concentrated on long-context loads.
Maya: running pod diagnostics now.
Maya: `kubectl -n inference get pods -l model=myri-7b-q2a -o wide` -> multiple CrashLoopBackOffs on nodes ip-10-11-5-{3,7}
Hector: throwing in logs from one of the pods.
Hector: ```
2026-06-11T15:12:04Z ERROR warmup: deserializing weights failed: DeserializationError: unexpected EOF
2026-06-11T15:12:04Z ERROR runtime: failed to migrate KV cache: cudaMemcpy failed: out of memory
2026-06-11T15:12:04Z INFO runtime: exiting with code 137
```
Maya: that matches — deserialization sometimes leaves partially-read tensors, then runtime tries to mmap/copy to GPU and OOMs. Could be corrupted model shard or a race in warmup path.
eng-runtime-oncall: pinging in. We saw a recent change to the fast-deser path in last deploy (PR #1129). Could be exposing partial reads under high fanout.
Maya: mitigation plan suggestion: 1) disable aggressive warmup for myri-7b-q2a, 2) route traffic to myri-7b-q2a-fallback (compat variant) for affected customers, 3) restart only healthy pods to drain bad ones, 4) if necessary, scale up fallback pool.
Elaine: CS note: customer alpha-payments reports intermittent failures; impact ~20% of their requests. I'll start a short status message to their AE.
Matt: I'm available to take a handoff in 15. Preparing to join.
Maya: performing step 1 now — toggling warmup flag for model.
Maya: `curl -X POST https://control-api/redwood/models/myri-7b-q2a/config -d '{"warmup_enabled":false}'` -> 200 OK
infra-bot: Rollout trigger: disabled warmup on myri-7b-q2a. change_id=chg-20260611-0901
Maya: step 2 — rerouting a small percent of traffic (10%) to myri-7b-q2a-fallback to observe behavior.
Maya: `admin-cli traffic-route set --model myri-7b-q2a --fallback myri-7b-q2a-fallback --percent 10 --region us-west-2`
Maya: initial metrics after 2m: error rate down from 9% -> 6%. pods still cycling but fewer OOMs in fallback.
eng-runtime-oncall: collecting core dumps and exact stack traces. Can someone capture a full failing pod log with env? command: `kubectl logs pod/<pod> -n inference --previous`
Hector: attached snippet of previous logs (pasted above) — looks like fast-deser read size mismatch: expected 512MB but got 0 bytes for shard-3.
eng-runtime-oncall: ok, pushing a hotfix candidate to revert fast-deser for warmup only. If we can keep warmup off we'll avoid the crash while we patch.
Maya: step 3 — draining CrashLoopBackOff pods. `kubectl cordon` unnecessary; just mark pods for replacement.
Maya: `kubectl delete pod <bad-pod> -n inference` -> recreated healthy instance without warmup flag, started OK.
Matt: joining. taking over incident. Handoff notes: warmup disabled, 10% traffic to fallback, customer alpha-payments impacted (~20% errors historically), root cause suspected: fast-deser race leading to partial shard reads + subsequent CUDA OOM during copy. eng-runtime working on revert patch, ETA 30-45m.
Matt: next actions for me: monitor error rate, increase fallback to 50% if errors don't decline, coordinate rollback of PR #1129 once patch ready, coordinate with infra for node-level checks.
Elaine: customer note drafted: "We're investigating increased 5xx on certain models in us-west-2. We've applied a mitigation routing and disabled warmup for the affected model. We're prioritizing a runtime patch. Will update in 30-60m." Approving to send now?
Maya: please send. include link to status page.
Elaine: sent message to AE + incident channel on CS side.
eng-runtime-oncall: quick status: reverted fast-deser in a canary runtime in staging; warmup path now uses legacy deserializer for canary. No regressions so far. Preparing to push patch to prod after test run.
Maya: infra checks: nodes that saw the crashes show higher GPU memory fragmentation. We triggered a soft reboot on node ip-10-11-5-7 to clear state. infra-bot reports node rejoined cluster.
infra-bot: node ip-10-11-5-7 marked healthy after kubelet restart.
Matt: increasing traffic to fallback to 50% now to protect customers while patch deploys.
Matt: `admin-cli traffic-route set --model myri-7b-q2a --fallback myri-7b-q2a-fallback --percent 50 --region us-west-2` -> 200 OK
Maya: after bump to 50%, 503s dropped to 1.5% over the last 5m for affected routes. alpha-payments reporting improvement.
eng-runtime-oncall: deploying revert patch to prod canary group now (10% of runtime infra). Will monitor for new failures.
Hector: leaving logs/attachments in incident ticket: stack traces, pod names, core dump ids: core-4435, core-4436.
eng-runtime-oncall: prod canary patched at 15:38 UTC. No warmup crashes seen in 8m. Proceeding with staged rollout 3x -> 30% -> 60%.
Matt: notifying SRE rotations and adding follow-ups: schedule thorough model shard checksum audit, add extra validation on deser reads, and add a metric for partial-shard reads.
Maya: handing off to Matt fully. My actions: disabled warmup, drained bad pods, scaled fallback to 50%, restarted affected node, validated lower error rate. Oncall handoff at 15:45 UTC.
Matt: taking it. I'll keep the incident open until the runtime patch fully rolled and we revert fallback traffic. I'll post updates on status page and coordinate postmortem.
Elaine: I'll update customers and log impact: total impacted requests ~12k over 45m, principal customer alpha-payments saw ~20% failure during peak window, currently stable.
Maya: thanks team. tagging this thread for postmortem owners: @eng-runtime-oncall and @Hector for troubleshooting writeup.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation active. warmup disabled, fallback routing 50%. assigned: Matt. severity: P2 -> monitoring.
Matt: will update again at next milestone (patch at 60% or 16:10 UTC).
--- end of thread content ---
